llm.summary: This travel expense helper stores trip spending records locally as expected, but users should understand those records can include private travel and financial details.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is travel expense tracking with currency conversion, summaries, and budget checks; the script implements only those functions using user-provided trip, amount, currency, category, description, and date fields.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses that accounting data is stored in the local travel_expenses/ directory, but it gives limited detail about retained fields, retention, deletion, or export controls.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No package installation, startup hook, system modification, network setup, or automatic execution is present in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local JSON storage of expense records is proportionate for this purpose, but the data may reveal spending, dates, and travel patterns on shared, backed-up, or synced machines.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The script persists records under the skill directory and creates files as needed, with no evidence of privilege escalation, background workers, credential access, remote transmission, or destructive behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with trip names, dates, amounts, categories, and descriptions being saved as local JSON files. On a shared or synced computer, review the travel_expenses/ directory and delete records when they are no longer needed.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: This is a valid privacy notice gap around local persistence, but the behavior is disclosed, purpose-aligned, locally scoped, and not enough to require Review by itself.
[VirusTotal] expected: Telemetry reports no malicious or suspicious engine detections and does not conflict with the artifact review.
[staticScan] expected: The static scan reported no suspicious patterns; manual inspection likewise found no network calls, shell execution, credential handling, or unrelated file access.
